subject: Best route for packaging rstan functionality

messages.author: 181bcebaf89c73b8
messages.subject: Best route for packaging rstan functionality
parts:
I have a stan model I would like to include in a package. It seems there could be two routes:
1. Include the .stan file as part of the package and arrange compilation at installation time somehow (doesn't seem like anyone does this - at least I don't see any .stan files in stanarm). 
2. Include stan generated C++ in /src, as discussed here: https://groups.google.com/forum/#!searchin/stan-users/R$20package/stan-users/UtNJZGtBstY/5kZ4nAQtBQAJ

Presumably 2 is the recommended approach? With 1 I'm not even sure how I would tell rstan to find the .stan file. 

Thanks!

David

messages.author: fc5d3270037d7478
messages.subject: Re: Best route for packaging rstan functionality
parts: On Thursday, February 4, 2016 at 1:43:54 PM UTC-5, David Knowles wrote:

I have a stan model I would like to include in a package. It seems there could be two routes:
1. Include the .stan file as part of the package and arrange compilation at installation time somehow (doesn't seem like anyone does this - at least I don't see any .stan files in stanarm).

rstanarm does do this. Where are you looking where you don't see any .stan files? If you look at the rstanarm GitHub repository the .stan files should be in the exec directory. Also, quoting from this post by Ben, 

The Makefile and cleanup scripts in the rstanarm package show how this can be accomplished (which took weeks to figure out), but it is easiest to get started by calling rstan::rstan_package_skeleton(), which sets up the package structure and copies some stuff from the rstanarm GitHub repository.

 That should help get you started.

messages.author: 181bcebaf89c73b8
messages.subject: Re: Best route for packaging rstan functionality
parts:
Hi all - so I finally got to doing this. Problems so far: 
- rstan.package.skeleton for some reason refused to find utils::package.skeleton in the eval(mc) call. I copied the rstan.package.skeleton into my own function and made a regular call to utils::package.skeleton. 
- make_cpp.R wasn't writing anything in src/, I think because I didn't have inst/chunks/license.stan. I got that from rstanarm. 

My problem now is that although Modules.cpp is being created (and looks fine at first glance), when .onLoad gets called in zzz.R I get the following: 

  call: value[[3L]](cond)
  error: failed to load module stan_fit4bb_glm_mod from package leafcutter
Failed to initialize module pointer: Error in FUN(X[[i]], ...): no such symbol _rcpp_module_boot_stan_fit4bb_glm_mod in package leafcutter

bb_glm is the name of one of my .stan models. 

Any help much appreciated!

messages.author: 181bcebaf89c73b8
messages.subject: Re: Best route for packaging rstan functionality
parts:
To add some more details: Ubuntu 14.04.4, R 3.2.3, rstan 2.9.0-3. 

I checked using 
objdump -T ....so | grep text
that the object it's claiming not to find (_rcpp_module_boot_stan_fit4bb_glm_mod) is really there in the package's dynamic library. 

I also checked that I could build the rstanarm package downloaded from github. 

Puzzling...

messages.author: 181bcebaf89c73b8
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Re: Best route for packaging rstan functionality
parts:
I think I got it: needed the following line in NAMESPACE:

useDynLib(mypackagename, .registration=TRUE)
On 24 February 2016 at 18:13, David Knowles <know...@gmail.com> wrote:

To add some more details: Ubuntu 14.04.4, R 3.2.3, rstan 2.9.0-3. 

I checked using 
objdump -T ....so | grep text
that the object it's claiming not to find (_rcpp_module_boot_stan_fit4bb_glm_mod) is really there in the package's dynamic library. 

I also checked that I could build the rstanarm package downloaded from github. 

Puzzling...

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Re: Best route for packaging rstan functionality
parts:
On Wednesday, February 24, 2016 at 9:53:18 PM UTC-5, David Knowles wrote:
I think I got it: needed the following line in NAMESPACE:

useDynLib(mypackagename, .registration=TRUE)

Yes, that is true. Since rstanarm uses roxygen to generate the NAMESPACE, I had overlooked that. I will add a sentence to that effect in the read-and-delete-me file.

Ben
